## Familiar Therapeutics Launches with $5 Million Seed to Close the Gap Between Human and Veterinary Medicine

2026-10-22 20:12 Last Updated At：20:40

  *   * REDWOOD CITY, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Oct 22, 2026--

Familiar Therapeutics launched today with $5 million in seed funding to bring the advances of modern human medicine to dogs and cats. The round was led by Pioneer Fund, Icehouse Ventures and BreakTHRU, a syndicate of animal-health industry leaders and veterinarians, with participation from angel investors.

This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261022813367/en/

Over the past two decades, a new generation of medicines has changed the outlook for people with chronic and life-threatening diseases. Dogs and cats develop many of the same diseases as people, often driven by the same underlying biology, yet very little of that medical progress has reached them. Fewer than 10 new drugs are approved by the FDA each year for companion animals, compared with more than 50 for people. For many serious conditions, veterinarians still rely on human medicines used off-label, without dosing or safety data for the species. Much of the science needed to change this exists, but adapting a drug for animals takes its own clinical studies, manufacturing work and FDA review. Without a dedicated path for that work, promising medicines rarely make it across to dogs and cats.

Familiar was built to close that gap. Because each program starts with years of human research behind it, Familiar aims to bring disease-modifying medicines to pets significantly faster than the seven to ten years a new animal drug typically takes. The company works with pharmaceutical and biotech partners on each program, licensing the veterinary rights to their drugs and leading the clinical development and manufacturing work needed for FDA approval in dogs and cats.

In the five months since its founding, Familiar built a pipeline of four lead programs and nine earlier-stage programs for dogs and cats, signed multiple partnership and licensing agreements with biopharmaceutical companies, opened two investigational new animal drug (INAD) files with the FDA Center for Veterinary Medicine and filed one provisional patent. The seed funding will move its lead programs into clinical studies and advance the rest of its pipeline.

Familiar was founded by serial entrepreneurs Elizabeth Iorns, PhD, and Dan Knox, MBA. They previously co-founded Science Exchange, the Y Combinator-backed R&D outsourcing platform used by the world's largest pharmaceutical companies, and led it through its acquisition in 2024. The gap between human and veterinary medicine became personal for Elizabeth in 2020, when her French Bulldog, Lily, was diagnosed with a terminal brain tumor. Elizabeth, a cancer biologist by training, worked through the research literature and found a checkpoint inhibitor that an academic team had tested in pet dogs with brain tumors, but no company had developed it for veterinary use. She and Dan licensed that therapy, partnered with Ardent Animal Health to combine it with their personalized cancer vaccine, and ran a registrational study in dogs with osteosarcoma that recently met its endpoint. Elizabeth and Dan founded Familiar to bring many more of these medicines to pets, leading their development through approval and launch across multiple therapeutic areas.

"Our goal is to give vets proven, FDA-approved treatments that change the course of serious diseases in dogs and cats, where today they often have very few options," said Elizabeth Iorns, co-founder and CEO of Familiar. "The science is often already there, and when you begin with a drug that already has years of human research behind it, the veterinary work can move much faster. Familiar is built to do that work all the way through to approval and commercialization, so those medicines can actually reach pets."

Familiar's most advanced program, FAM-010, targets hemangiosarcoma, one of the most aggressive cancers in dogs and a disease with no FDA-approved treatment. With surgery alone, median survival is under two months. Familiar is working toward making FAM-010 the first FDA-approved treatment for hemangiosarcoma in dogs, starting this fall with a pilot study at the University of Illinois College of Veterinary Medicine, led by Timothy M. Fan, DVM, PhD.

Familiar's other lead programs target intervertebral disc disease, a common cause of back pain and paralysis in dogs; breathing disorders in flat-faced breeds such as French Bulldogs and Pugs; and immune-mediated diseases. Every program is designed for full FDA approval. Where a program qualifies, Familiar may also seek conditional approval, which lets veterinarians use a drug for a serious unmet need while the final effectiveness studies are completed.

"The science flows both ways," said Dan Knox, co-founder and COO of Familiar. "When we develop a drug for dogs and cats with naturally occurring disease, the evidence we generate can also inform and de-risk our biopharma partners' human programs. Those partners keep their human rights and share in veterinary sales, so they earn a faster return on research they've already paid for. That's a big part of why we've been able to sign partners so quickly."

Familiar's team includes senior animal-health drug developers who have contributed to more than 30 FDA approvals across decades of combined experience at companies including Zoetis, Elanco, and Bayer Animal Health. Familiar also has a 12-member Scientific Advisory Board which brings together veterinary specialists, practicing veterinarians and animal-health researchers.

"Elizabeth and Dan are two of New Zealand's most accomplished founders," said Robbie Paul, CEO of Icehouse Ventures. "The market for veterinary medicines is growing, and pet owners now expect the same standard of care for their animals that they get themselves. We have high conviction that Elizabeth, Dan and their team are the right people to close the gap between human and veterinary medicine, and we're proud to have been Familiar's first institutional investor."

Veterinarians and pet owners can learn more about the FAM-010 study at familiartx.com/studies/fam-010. Pharmaceutical and biotech companies interested in partnering with Familiar can contact partnerships@familiartx.com.

About Familiar Therapeutics

Familiar Therapeutics is a biotechnology company bringing medicines first developed for people to dogs and cats. The company licenses veterinary rights to drugs with years of human research behind them, then leads the veterinary development and regulatory work needed to bring them to pets, with the goal of advancing selected programs significantly faster than typical animal drug development. Familiar was founded in May 2026 by Elizabeth Iorns and Dan Knox. The company is based in Redwood City, California, and is backed by Pioneer Fund, Icehouse Ventures, BreakTHRU and other investors. Learn more at familiartx.com.

FAM-010 and all other Familiar programs are investigational and have not been approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. FDA approval is not guaranteed.

Forward-looking statements

This press release contains forward-looking statements, including statements about Familiar's development programs, planned clinical studies, regulatory plans and the timing of these activities. These statements involve risks and uncertainties, and actual results may differ materially. Familiar undertakes no obligation to update these statements.

# Familiar Therapeutics Launches With $5 Million In Seed Funding

By Amit Chowdhry Yesterday at 4:16 PM

Familiar Therapeutics Launches With $5 Million In Seed Funding

Familiar Therapeutics, a Redwood City, California-based biotechnology company developing treatments for companion animals, has launched with $5 million in seed funding to adapt advances in human medicine for dogs and cats. The financing was led by Pioneer Fund, Icehouse Ventures, and BreakTHRU, an investment syndicate comprising animal health industry leaders and veterinarians, with additional participation from angel investors.

Founded in May 2026 by entrepreneurs Elizabeth Iorns and Dan Knox, Familiar is developing a portfolio of veterinary medicines based on drugs that have already undergone substantial research for human diseases.

The company aims to address the gap between advances in human therapeutics and the limited treatment options available for pets suffering from serious illnesses.

Although dogs and cats can develop many of the same diseases as humans, relatively few new medications are approved specifically for companion animals each year. Familiar noted that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration approves fewer than 10 new companion animal drugs annually, compared with more than 50 for human use.

As a result, veterinarians frequently rely on medications developed for humans, sometimes without comprehensive dosing or safety data specific to the animal species being treated.

Familiar intends to address this challenge by licensing veterinary rights to promising treatments from pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies, then conducting the animal-specific research, manufacturing development, and regulatory work required for veterinary approval.

By building on existing human research, the company believes it can accelerate development compared with the seven to ten years typically required to bring a new animal medicine to market.

During its first five months, Familiar established a pipeline of 13 programs, comprising four lead candidates and nine earlier-stage projects. The portfolio spans oncology, neurology, cardiology, respiratory conditions, and immunology.

The company has also established several pharmaceutical partnerships, filed a provisional patent, and opened two investigational new animal drug files with the FDA’s Center for Veterinary Medicine.

Its most advanced program, FAM-010, is being developed to treat hemangiosarcoma, an aggressive cancer affecting dogs for which no FDA-approved treatment currently exists.

Familiar plans to begin a pilot clinical study of FAM-010 at the University of Illinois College of Veterinary Medicine in fall 2026. The study will be led by Timothy M. Fan, DVM, PhD.

Other lead programs address intervertebral disc disease, which can cause pain and paralysis in dogs; respiratory disorders affecting flat-faced breeds such as French Bulldogs and Pugs; and immune-mediated diseases.

The company intends to pursue FDA approval for its programs and may seek conditional approval where permitted for treatments addressing serious unmet veterinary needs.

Iorns and Knox previously co-founded Science Exchange, a Y Combinator-backed research and development outsourcing platform acquired in 2024.

Their interest in veterinary therapeutics was influenced by Iorns’ experience seeking treatment for her French Bulldog, Lily, following a terminal brain tumor diagnosis in 2020.

That work eventually contributed to a collaboration involving a checkpoint inhibitor and a personalized cancer vaccine developed with Ardent Animal Health. A subsequent registrational study involving dogs with osteosarcoma recently met its endpoint.

Familiar has assembled an animal health development team with experience contributing to more than 30 FDA approvals at companies including Zoetis, Elanco, and Bayer Animal Health. It also maintains a 12-member scientific advisory board.

The $5 million seed investment will support clinical development of Familiar’s lead programs and continued advancement of its broader pipeline.

All Familiar drug candidates remain investigational and have not received FDA approval.

KEY QUOTES:

“Our goal is to give vets proven, FDA-approved treatments that change the course of serious diseases in dogs and cats, where today they often have very few options. The science is often already there, and when you begin with a drug that already has years of human research behind it, the veterinary work can move much faster. Familiar is built to do that work all the way through to approval and commercialization, so those medicines can actually reach pets.”

Elizabeth Iorns, Co-Founder And CEO Of Familiar Therapeutics

“The science flows both ways. When we develop a drug for dogs and cats with naturally occurring disease, the evidence we generate can also inform and de-risk our biopharma partners’ human programs. Those partners keep their human rights and share in veterinary sales, so they earn a faster return on research they’ve already paid for. That’s a big part of why we’ve been able to sign partners so quickly.”

Dan Knox, Co-Founder And COO Of Familiar Therapeutics

“Elizabeth and Dan are two of New Zealand’s most accomplished founders. The market for veterinary medicines is growing, and pet owners now expect the same standard of care for their animals that they get themselves. We have high conviction that Elizabeth, Dan and their team are the right people to close the gap between human and veterinary medicine, and we’re proud to have been Familiar’s first institutional investor.”

Phase 1 trials are typically conducted in a small group of animals (6-12) with cancer to test a new treatment that has never been tried in a clinical patient. The goals are to evaluate safety and side effects, and to determine the dose and way to use the treatment. It is important to remember that no therapeutic benefit is expected in a phase 1 trial.

Phase 2 trials use information from phase 1 trials to use the new treatment at a given dose and schedule in a larger group of animals with cancer (usually 20-40). The goal of a phase 2 trial is to determine efficacy of the new treatment and further evaluate safety. In cancer clinical trials, a phase 2 trial is intended to determine what types of cancer will respond or how well a given cancer responds to a new therapy.

Phase 3 trials compare the new treatment to standard treatment options in a large group of animals with cancer. The goal is to determine whether the new treatment is better than other common treatments and to further monitor safety and side effects.

Phase 4 trials compare two or more well-established treatment regimes in a given group of patients, typically after the treatment has already been approved for use (in people) or in common use (in animals).

A Source of Inspiration: A Retired Military Dog. K500 Turbo. A Hero.

The MiliDog Program was created to fill an existing void to provide cancer care for Retired Military Dogs, and Contract Working Dogs nationwide. These elite warriors are expected to work in the most austere of environments and face conditions that most human beings cannot survive. The K-9 units are vital in ensuring the success of every mission and operate in all conditions. Our mission is to ensure that every single elite warrior has a chance in a battle against cancer.

## Join our clinical-trial network.

Familiar's trials are designed to run in client-owned animals with naturally occurring disease, generating evidence in the patients veterinarians see every day.

We're building a network of general practices and specialty centers to support these studies as our programs advance.

As studies open across our therapeutic areas, network practices will be among the first we contact about opportunities to participate.

### What participation looks like

#### Familiar-funded

We sponsor and fund the study.

#### Client-owned patients

Trials enroll animals with naturally occurring disease treated in clinical practice.

#### Clinically grounded protocols

Studies are designed with our Scientific Advisory Board and participating investigators.
